title: Why Use a MARISA Trie from DuckDB?
description: Build one BLOB from a column of strings, then run membership tests, autocomplete prefix searches, and longest-prefix matches against it — in O(|key|), independent of dictionary size. The static-trie companion to [`bitfilters`](/products/extensions/bitfilters): both answer set-membership questions, but a [MARISA trie](https://github.com/s-yata/marisa-trie) keeps the strings and supports prefix queries.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Big static string sets — English wordlists, city/airport names, IP-CIDR labels, URL routing tables, autocomplete dictionaries — packed into a single self-contained BLOB you can store in any DuckDB column.

bulletPoints.label: Autocomplete and type-ahead
bulletPoints.description: [`marisa_predictive`](#marisa_predictive) returns every entry that starts with a given prefix, capped at `max_results`. One BLOB, microsecond lookups — drop it behind a search box without standing up a separate service.

bulletPoints.label: Spell-check and dictionary lookups
bulletPoints.description: [`marisa_lookup`](#marisa_lookup) is a BOOLEAN “is this exact string in the set?” test. Smaller and prefix-aware where a hash set or [`bitfilters`](/products/extensions/bitfilters) Bloom would otherwise live.

bulletPoints.label: Longest-prefix-match routing
bulletPoints.description: [`marisa_common_prefix`](#marisa_common_prefix) returns every string in the trie that is itself a prefix of the query string — the primitive behind URL routers, IP-CIDR label tables, and rule lookups.

bulletPoints.label: Compact dictionary side of a join
bulletPoints.description: Materialize one trie per partition / day / tenant at write time and ship the BLOB — a [Patricia trie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radix_tree) of prefix-rich data is dramatically smaller than the equivalent flat string list.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: MARISA — *Matching Algorithm with Recursively Implemented StorAge* — is a [succinct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succinct_data_structure) static [Patricia/radix trie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radix_tree) maintained for over a decade as [`s-yata/marisa-trie`](https://github.com/s-yata/marisa-trie). This extension is a thin DuckDB wrapper over that library.

bulletPoints.label: One aggregate, one BLOB
bulletPoints.description: [`marisa_trie`](#marisa_trie) is the only constructor — an aggregate over a `VARCHAR` column that emits a single self-contained `BLOB`. Store it in any column type, persist to Parquet, ship to another DuckDB instance.

bulletPoints.label: Three query primitives
bulletPoints.description: [`marisa_lookup`](#marisa_lookup) (exact membership), [`marisa_predictive`](#marisa_predictive) (“starts with”), and [`marisa_common_prefix`](#marisa_common_prefix) (“is a prefix of”). All read the BLOB directly — no decode or warm-up step.

bulletPoints.label: O(|key|), not O(|dictionary|)
bulletPoints.description: Lookup work scales with the length of the search key, not the size of the trie. The first query is as fast as the millionth, whether the dictionary holds a thousand strings or ten million.

bulletPoints.label: Prefix-rich data wins big
bulletPoints.description: URLs, paths, names, and dictionary words share enormous prefix structure — a typical English wordlist of ~470K entries fits in around 800 KB, roughly a fifth the size of the same words as a flat sorted list.

sections.title: When to choose something else
sections.description: MARISA is a sharp, narrow tool. Knowing where it isn't the right fit is half the value.

bulletPoints.label: Static — no incremental insert or delete
bulletPoints.description: Once built, the trie is immutable. Updates require rebuilding from the source set. For a 470K-entry dictionary that's milliseconds; for billions, plan accordingly.

bulletPoints.label: String keys only
bulletPoints.description: No numeric or composite keys. `VARCHAR` in, `VARCHAR` out. Encode integers as text upstream if you must, or pick a different index.

bulletPoints.label: Random unrelated strings: prefer a hash or filter
bulletPoints.description: Without shared prefixes, the trie loses its compression edge. For pure membership tests on uncorrelated keys, [`bitfilters`](/products/extensions/bitfilters) (Bloom / XOR / Binary Fuse) is smaller and just as fast — but it can't return the strings or answer prefix queries.

bulletPoints.label: Lexicographic order only
bulletPoints.description: If you need a different ordering at query time, build separate tries. The trie itself is fixed at lexicographic key order.

useCases.title: Autocomplete backend in SQL
useCases.description: Build [`marisa_trie`](#marisa_trie) over your search corpus once at ingest time, store the BLOB, and serve type-ahead requests with [`marisa_predictive`](#marisa_predictive) directly from DuckDB — no separate Elasticsearch / Trie service for static dictionaries.

useCases.title: Spell-check / dictionary membership
useCases.description: An English wordlist or domain-specific term list compiled into a trie BLOB you can ship inside a Parquet file. Pair with [`fuzzycomplete`](/products/extensions/fuzzycomplete) or [`rapidfuzz`](/products/extensions/rapidfuzz) for fuzzy fallbacks when exact lookup misses.

useCases.title: Routing and longest-prefix-match tables
useCases.description: URL paths, feature-flag rules, geo / CIDR labels — anywhere you ask "which rules match this input?" Use [`marisa_common_prefix`](#marisa_common_prefix) against a trie of the rule keys.

useCases.title: Compact join dictionary
useCases.description: Materialize one trie per partition or per day at write time. The BLOB ships smaller than the underlying string list, decompresses to nothing (it's already mmap-ready), and serves prefix and membership queries from the same blob.
